summary: Avista said it is taking more time to evaluate energy requests from new large data center developers and paused negotiations under its MOU with a 125-500 MW data center developer.
notes: 8-K Ex. 99.1 (2026-06-12); Q2 10-Q (filed 2026-08-03) still describes the pause. Scope ambiguous: release covers processing of requests from new large data center developers, Spokesman reads it as the one 500 MW MOU. Possible site: former Kaiser smelter, Mead (Spokane County). Avista serves eastern WA, northern ID and part of MT; county field lists only the site county. No resumption found as of 2026-10-07.

summary: City-owned TVA distributor announced a moratorium on entertaining proposals for new data center projects in its service area, including one it was considering in south Johnson City.
notes: Utility statement quoted by WCYB/WJHL 2025-05-13 ("the costs currently outweigh the benefits"); no board vote or end date found. Context: Limestone bitcoin mine served by BrightRidge closing by March 2026 under a settlement; the south JC site may have been for crypto. Separate from upstream Johnson City (city land-use moratorium 2025-06-05). Status after May 2025 not verified. County list approximate.

jurisdiction_name: Silicon Valley Power (City of Santa Clara electric utility)
summary: City-owned utility stopped accepting new data center load applications in 2023 because requests exceeded capacity, pending a ~$450M system upgrade; the pause remained in effect in Oct 2026.
notes: KTVU 2026-10-06 read in full. City news release (santaclaraca.gov, 403 to fetch) quoted in search snippets: SVP "stopped accepting new data center requests in 2023" and "the pause in electrical load applications for new data centers remains in effect". Start month not found. Not a land-use moratorium; Santa Clara is not in upstream.

summary: Village trustees adopted a two-year moratorium on cryptocurrency, blockchain and similar data-mining operations after dozens of requests drawn by the village utility's low-cost NYPA hydropower.
notes: Press-Republican 2018-05-28; GovTech 2018-04-23 already reported a temporary ban, so adoption may be April 2018. A village local law (civil penalties up to $1,000/day), like the pass-1 Plattsburgh row; may belong in the city slice. End not found; expired assumed (~mid-2020).

jurisdiction_name: Village of Lake Placid (Lake Placid Village, Inc. electric)
summary: Village of Lake Placid and Town of North Elba approved an 18-month moratorium on cryptomining, citing the village utility's cheap hydropower and Plattsburgh's experience.
notes: Adirondack Daily Enterprise 2018-05-09: both boards approved; effective within 30 days of filing. A local law, may belong in the city slice (as Plattsburgh). Pass 2 cites Times Union 2019-03-08 saying the mayor expected it to be lifted; end not confirmed; expired assumed (~late 2019).

summary: Village board adopted Local Law #1-2024, a moratorium on commercial cryptocurrency mining, at the electric superintendent's urging to keep the village's cheap power for residents.
notes: Board minutes 2024-03-18: hearing on a moratorium "within the Village and Town of Tupper Lake", motion carried 5-0. The superintendent spoke of revisiting the local law, which implies an earlier one (2018?). Duration and end not found; expired assumed. Local law, may belong in city slice. Separate Town of Tupper Lake 12-month data center/crypto moratorium (hearing 2026-09-21) is a land-use lead, not in upstream.
